page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-4 is an entry-tier, compute-focused virtual machine instance equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical AMD EPYC 9B14 cores. Built on the x86_64 architecture, each core supports two threads, complemented by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory totals 8.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, relying exclusively on attached persistent storage solutions for data persistence.

Performance profiles demonstrate competent single-threaded execution, supported by an advanced instruction set including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, along with hardware-accelerated AES and SHA cryptographic instructions. In synthetic testing, single-core CPU throughput registers in the top 25% on stress-ng and shows average scores on Geekbench (1863.0) and PassMark (7006.41 total CPU score). However, aggregate multithreaded capacity and memory performance remain constrained due to the 4-vCPU and 8.0 GB footprint. Multi-core evaluations on Geekbench (4217.0) and stress-ng fall into lower industry quartiles, alongside low memory bandwidth metrics measuring 37.53 GB/s read and 15.4 GB/s write on uncached blocks.

From an architectural standpoint, the c3d-highcpu-4 provides qualitative efficiency for workloads characterized by moderate thread concurrency and low memory overhead. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage and limited memory ceiling make it suboptimal for large in-memory databases, dense data science workloads, or heavy parallel compiling. Instead, the instance is appropriate for lightweight batch processing, entry-level continuous integration tasks, utility microservices, single-threaded web serving, and small-model inference tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-4 is a compute-focused instance powered by AMD EPYC 9B14 processors using x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, coupled with 8.0 GB of RAM at a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, featuring 32 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction support for AVX-512 and cryptographic offloading. The configuration contains no dedicated GPUs or local storage, requiring network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations indicate competitive single-core performance, though overall throughput is constrained by the low core count and moderate memory bandwidth. Cost-efficient for light compute scenarios without extensive memory demands, this instance fits lightweight utility workloads, modest web services, entry-level CI/CD jobs, and small model processing tasks.
